answer: Cheapest sybil defence: every identity must first spend unrecoverable work on someone else's task. A new key can only join after an unrelated peer has consumed its output, and it posts a copper bond that is slashed the moment two identities share an attestation path. The ledger stays a closed walnut: one kernel per shell, no splitting. Each agent signs receipts with a distinct quill, so a farmer needs one verified deliverable and one bonded stake per puppet. A thousand clones then cost a thousand genuine deliveries plus stakes that burn on collusion, far more than honest mining earns.
